subject: LLM data usage commitments and operational evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novomed.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novomed.com, security@novomed.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify training prohibition + operational evidence

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we move to procurement, our legal and security teams need a clear, auditable confirmation that any data sent to Redwood's hosted API for NovoMed will not be used to improve or train models (no-learning). Specifically we need:

- A short explanation of how "no-learning" is enforced in hosted mode (flags, isolates, KV caching behavior).
- A list of subprocessors and which regions they operate in.
- Evidence we can consume: an ops checklist, export paths (SFTP/API), and an attestation we can include in our DPA.
- Clarification on prompt/response ownership: will NovoMed retain exclusive rights to outputs and stored prompts?

Could you also review the attached DPA redlines (I've attached an initial markup)? We need enough to move procurement and SOC2 scope review.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Security, NovoMed
[attachment: NovoMed_DPA_redlines_20260829.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novomed.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training prohibition + operational evidence

Elena — thanks for the note and the redlines. Short answers up front:

- No-learning: For hosted API we honor customer-configured no-training flags. Requests tagged as 'no_train' are routed to a serving path that does not write user prompts/responses to persistent training stores. We also provide an optional ephemeral KV cache mode and TTL-based retention controls.

- Subprocessors: I'll attach our current inventory and a spreadsheet of questions for you.

- Evidence: We can provide an ops checklist (how exports are produced, retention settings), an export path (SFTP/API export workflows), and a signed attestation from our legal team confirming that data marked no-train will not be used for model improvement. SOC2 artifacts require our formal attestation process; we can provide the SOC2 cover letter and a scope statement.

- Prompt/response ownership: Our standard position is that customers retain output rights for their tenant data. We'll confirm the exact DPA language you want.

I'm looping in Grace from Privacy/Ops and David from Legal to assemble the evidence pack. We'll aim to surface the inventory and checklist within 3 business days and a signed attestation within one week.

Attachments: "redwood-subprocessor-inventory-20260828.csv" (current inventory).

Next steps: Grace and David — can you confirm the checklist items and whether we can provide a GC-signed attestation by next Tuesday?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novomed.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training prohibition + operational evidence

Hi Elena / Marissa,

Quick technical operations summary to supplement Marissa's note: 

1) Enforcement model: Requests with the no-train flag are processed by a runtime path that disables telemetry writes to our model-improvement pipeline. There is a runtime guard (audit-logged) that prevents the data from reaching the model training queue.

2) Cache and retention: We support ephemeral KV sessions (default TTL configurable per tenant) and a tenant-level retention policy. For hosted customers who opt-out of training we can set prompt logs to a 0- or 7-day retention, depending on the export/retention SLA.

3) Isolation options: If your security team prefers, we can route traffic to Dedicated capacity or Private deployment (VPC) to provide stronger isolation and onshore key management.

4) Exports & proofs: Exports are generated via a signed SFTP job or a secure API pull (mutual TLS). We can provide a checklist describing the export generation, hashing, signing, and proof-of-deletion steps.

I'll attach the ops checklist draft and the export workflow diagram. If you require a specific onshore KMS assertion, we can add that to the evidence pack and map subprocessors by region.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Privacy & Trust, Redwood
[attachment: ops-evidence-checklist.md (text/markdown)]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novomed.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novomed.com, security@novomed.com, legal@novomed.com
Date: 2026-08-31T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training prohibition + operational evidence

Marissa / Grace — thanks for the quick response and the inventory. A few clarifying asks from our side after a first pass of the materials:

- Can you provide a signed attestation from Redwood's GC that "data marked no-train will not be used for model improvement," and include the exact service paths that are blocked? We need language we can attach to the DPA.
- We require a subprocessor map that includes whether subprocessors process data outside the US and the contractual flow (who can access logs). Please add column for "onshore processing" for EU/US/APAC.
- We will propose three short DPA edits: (1) explicit no-training clause, (2) explicit output ownership clause, and (3) proof-of-deletion timeline for prompt logs. I've attached our redline PDF.

Also: SOC2 scope — can you indicate whether user prompt logs are in-scope for SOC2 and whether the attestation can reference SOC2 controls?

I'll schedule a quick call with procurement/security for next Thursday to finalize acceptance criteria.

Elena
[attachment: NovoMed_DPA_redlines_20260829.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novomed.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training prohibition + operational evidence

Elena — appreciate the redlines. We can provide the following: 

- A GC-signed attestation that data explicitly labeled "no_train" will not be ingested into our model improvement pipelines. The attestation will reference the internal runtime mechanism that enforces this and will be accompanied by a short schematic of blocked service paths.
- Subprocessor map with onshore/region columns: we'll provide a CSV export that marks processing region and access level.
- SOC2: Prompt logs are not part of our standard public SOC2 report by default. However, we can provide a scoped control statement — i.e., a SOC2 cover letter summarizing whether tenant logging is included in the controls we test.

Draft timeline:
- By 2026-09-03: deliver subprocessor CSV and ops checklist draft.
- By 2026-09-06: GC-signed attestation and draft DPA language incorporating the three edits you flagged.

If those dates work, we'll prepare the evidence pack and join the Thursday call. For the DPA edits we generally prefer narrow operational language rather than absolute IP assignments; happy to take your exact proposed text and provide redlines.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
